test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following services was NOT present in India for the common man at the time of Independence?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Call centres__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Call centres service **was** NOT **present in India for **the common man at the time of Independence.**
 
• **India **started to become a popular location for **call centres** that engage with consumers who are based in developed markets that speak** English, like the US, the UK, and Australia, around 1999–2000.**
 
• Since then, the call centre work of the vast majority of consumer companies on the Fortune 500 list has been outsourced to India, and it has been a wonderful growth story. A multi-billion dollar industry has been developed in India around it.
 
• **In 1998, Mr Bhasin **established the nation's first call centre with only 18 workers fielding calls in a space where booths were divided by saris suspended from the ceiling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India Post, **a division of the Department of Post under the Ministry of Communications, is a postal service that is run by the government.
 
• It is the most widely used postal system in the entire globe and is commonly referred to as the Post Office. In 1766, Warren Hastings undertook the initiative on behalf of the East India Company to launch the nation's first postal service. When it first started, it was known as "Company Mail."
 
• From Calcutta to Diamond Harbour, the first experimental **electric telegraph **connection was established.
 
• It was made available to the British East India Company in 1851.
 
• For telegraph facilities, a separate department was established in 1854. The Indian Telegraph Act was first introduced in India in 1885. 
 
• **The first passenger train** travelled the 34 km route between Thane and Bori Bunder on April 16, 1853.
 
• It had thirteen carriages and was driven by three engines with the names Sahib, Sultan, and Sindh.
